sections.h2: Where do you take a Warren County tax payment?
sections.html:
Find the Warren County tax office at 117 S. Main St. in Warrenton, 27589, beside the courthouse. Mail goes to PO Box 240, Warrenton, NC 27589. Most national holidays are observed.

Some routes carry fees, so know the free ones.

  • Phone 1-866-483-9680 or use warren.webtaxpay.com. Printed charges: debit card $3.95, credit card 2.60 percent of the amount, check or eCheck $2.50.
  • A mailed check costs nothing.
  • The drop box right of the office door is also free.

The tax administrator answers to the commissioners and the county manager, and also to the state Department of Revenue and Property Tax Commission.

sections.h2: What rate does Warren County list for 2026-2027?
sections.html:
Warren's Tax Administrator page prints $0.5950 per $100 as the county rate on real and personal property for 2026-2027. Budget-season documents can show different figures, so confirm the rate with the tax office before relying on it.

Warren last revalued in 2025. Those assessments remain until 2032 unless an owner adds something such as a garage, room or new house, and the next revaluation is slated for 2033. A private appraisal company assists the county.

That long gap affects a sale: a buyer's tax value stays on the 2025 appraisal, whatever the contract price, until the building changes.

sections.h2: When does Warren County interest start?
sections.html:
The 2026 bills are due September 1 but not delinquent until January 6, 2027, so January 5 is the last clean day. Then 2 percent applies for January, plus three-fourths of one percent for each later month.

The county's calendar shows what follows if you fall behind.

Warren County yearly tax steps
WhenWhat happens
January 1Ownership and value fixed; real property appeals open
January 6Interest starts; enforced collection, up to foreclosure, follows
January 31Listing period ends; 10 percent late penalty
March and AprilLetters in March; unpaid accounts advertised in April
June 1Relief applications due
AugustAnnual tax bills mailed
September 1Current year taxes due

sections.h2: Can a Warren County deed be recorded with taxes owed?
sections.html:
Only with a tax certification or an attorney's statement. Since January 7, 2026, a commissioners' resolution under G.S. 161-31 bars the Register of Deeds from accepting a transfer deed unless the Tax Collector certifies that no delinquent taxes are a lien.

The alternative is a statement added by the closing attorney that delinquent taxes will be paid at closing. Bring the deed to the Tax Collector between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. so staff can research the parcel and stamp it if warranted.

Check the tax account well before closing. Several unpaid years do not block a sale, but the arrears come out of proceeds and the office needs research time.

sections.h2: How does a Warren County value appeal work?
sections.html:
Each January 1 opens the real property appeal window, which closes when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns. The 2026 window closed May 18, 2026; the 2027 window opens January 1, 2027, with an informal appeal form posted under Forms.

Statute puts the board's first meeting between the first Mondays of April and May. Ask for your hearing before adjournment. A losing owner has 30 days from the mailed decision to notify the Property Tax Commission.

Warren adds two points. The owner bears the burden of showing a substantial overstatement, and market-value arguments are allowed only in a revaluation year. Vehicles, boats, trailers, aircraft and business equipment follow a different clock: 30 days from receiving the bill.

sections.h2: What are the steps of a Warren County value appeal, and what evidence counts?
sections.html:
The county's appeal page sets a three-step path: informal appeal, formal appeal and the state Property Tax Commission. File a separate informal appeal form for each parcel, give your own opinion of value, and attach support for it.

  • Recent sales offered as support must have closed before the 1/1/2025 effective date of the revaluation. Sales since then do not count.
  • Appraisals, photos of deferred maintenance and contractor estimates can go with the form.
  • Attorneys and tax representatives must supply a Power of Attorney.
  • Arguments based on the percentage increase from the last appraisal, the tax bill's size, economic conditions or the owner's ability to pay are not grounds for appeal.

If the informal review does not satisfy you, the formal appeal goes to the Board of Equalization and Review, which the county calls a quasi-judicial setting where taxpayers give sworn testimony. A formal appeal filed after the board adjourns is heard the following tax year. From there, the Property Tax Commission requires Form AV-14, received or postmarked within 30 days of the board's mailed decision, and non-attorney representatives file Form AV-63.

The county also notes that the prior revaluation was effective 1/1/2017, so the 2025 change reflected eight years of market movement in one step.

sections.h2: What listing and farm-use rules matter in Warren County?
sections.html:
Personal and business personal property is listed each January 1 to 31, with a 10 percent penalty for lateness. The county's list includes single wide mobile homes, farm equipment, unregistered vehicles, boats, aircraft, billboards and short-term rentals.

Real property stays listed permanently, so no yearly relisting unless something changed. Request extensions by January 31; mailed listings need a postmark by then, or April 15 with an extension. Get a mailing receipt.

Present use value matters to owners of working land. The county's minimums:

  • Agricultural land: at least ten acres in commercial production of crops or animals.
  • Forest land: at least twenty acres meeting the forest requirements.
  • Horticultural land: at least five acres in commercial production of fruits, vegetables, nursery or floral products.
  • Agricultural and horticultural income: an average gross of $1,000 per year over three years; forest land has no income test.

Applications are due January 31. A buyer must apply within sixty days of a transfer, so mention enrollment to the buyer's attorney.

sections.h2: What happens if a Warren County owner stays behind on tax?
sections.html:
Collection steps begin after January 6, and the county's calendar runs from letters to a newspaper notice. Delinquent tax letters are mailed in March, and accounts still unpaid at the end of that month are advertised in the local paper in April. The tax office says enforced collection, up to and including foreclosure, can follow.

State law supports that. The tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date, with penalties, interest and costs added, and the county can bring a foreclosure action in the county where the property lies. A sale goes to the highest bidder at the courthouse door, where the commissioner may ask for a deposit of up to 20 percent of the bid. Exceptions or an increased bid may be filed within 10 days after the report of sale. A person redeeming before confirmation pays all taxes plus penalties, interest and costs.

An owner who sells first avoids that sequence entirely. Call the Warrenton tax office, learn the balance, and ask your closing attorney to arrange payment at closing.

sections.h2: What relief can Warren County owners claim?
sections.html:
Older, disabled and veteran owners can apply by June 1. Seniors 65 and over can collect an application from January 2, and disability or disabled veteran applicants add the A-9A or NCDVA-9 form.

The state's terms: $25,000 or half of appraised value, whichever is greater, for the elderly or disabled, with a $38,800 income limit for 2026; and $45,000 off for disabled veterans without age or income tests. Only one of the three programs may be used. The county describes present use value savings of up to 90 percent.

If you inherited a Warren County house, ask the tax office whether a new application is needed.

faqs.q: When does Warren County tax interest begin?
faqs.a: January 6, 2027 for the 2026 bills. January 5 is the last interest-free day.

faqs.q: Does Warren County check taxes before recording a deed?
faqs.a: Yes, or an attorney's statement that delinquent taxes will be paid at closing, under a resolution effective January 7, 2026.

faqs.q: How can I pay Warren County tax free of fees?
faqs.a: By mailed check or the drop box at 117 S. Main St.; card and eCheck payments carry fees.

faqs.q: When is Warren County's next revaluation?
Can I still appeal my 2026 Warren County value?
faqs.a: The 2026 window closed May 18, 2026, and the 2027 window opens January 1, 2027.
